tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

## Abstract

We report the mean drag and in-line force fluctuations of smooth circular cylinders of
diameter D = 25.4, 38.1 and 50.8 mm towed through a water tank with a fixed
submerged length of 0.60 m. The Reynolds number spans 4.7 × 10³ ≤ Re ≤ 5.0 × 10⁴. Forces

independent of Re and D. Both results are consistent with classical subcritical-regime

number St ≈ 0.2 (Roshko 1961; Achenbach 1968; Zdravkovich 1997; Norberg 2003)

in this range serve two purposes. They benchmark a facility and its force-measurement chain,
and they provide reference data for configurations that depart from the ideal
two-dimensional cylinder. Examples include finite immersion, a free surface and moderate blockage.

*Blockage.* The geometric blockage ratio is 2.3–4.5 %. Blockage increases the measured

cylinder. Applying a standard correction (e.g. Allen & Vincenti 1944; Maskell 1963; West &

*Free surface.* The cylinders pierce the free surface. The diameter Froude number
Fr_D = U/√(gD) reaches 2.2 for the 25.4 mm cylinder, high enough for a bow wave and
ventilated wake to form near the surface [TODO: observations or photos?]. The added

with speed for the smaller cylinders, but the present data cannot separate it from
Re. A test at fixed Re and varying Fr_D (e.g. different water temperatures or
immersion depths) would distinguish the two.

local sectional drag over a few diameters (Zdravkovich 1997 **[CHECK]**). For L/D = 12–24 this
effect would bias the total C_D low relative to 2D values, partly offsetting blockage.

Each condition was towed once. The three diameters were tested on different dates, with
different water temperatures and, for D = 38.1 mm, after the load cell was remounted and
recalibrated. Diameter is therefore confounded with test campaign. That the three
campaigns agree within 1.3 % is itself evidence of good reproducibility. Repeat tows and
at least one diameter repeated across campaigns would strengthen the paper considerably.

import pandas as pd

FS = 200.0
EXCLUDE = {17: "zero drifted ~4.2 N during/after run"}

MARKERS = {"1in": "o", "1.5in": "s", "2in": "^"}

LABELS = {"1in": "D = 25.4 mm", "1.5in": "D = 38.1 mm", "2in": "D = 50.8 mm"}

    # Tanaka et al. (2001), kg/m^3
    a1, a2, a3, a4, a5 = -3.983035, 301.797, 522528.9, 69.34881, 999.974950
    return a5 * (1 - (T + a1) ** 2 * (T + a2) / (a3 * (T + a4)))

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

# Reproduces every number, table and figure in paper/draft.md from the raw data.
# Run from the project root:  python paper/make_paper_results.py
#
# Differences from process.py / process_b3.py / analysis.ipynb:
#   - one loader for both DAQ formats; reads the local data/raw tree
#   - March sensitivity fitted from loadcell_2026-03.csv (0.021292 V/N)
#     rather than the rounded 0.0213 (changes forces by 0.04%)
#   - water density and viscosity evaluated at the logged temperature of
#     each run instead of fixed 20 C values
#   - run 17 excluded (zero drift during the run, see notes.md)
#   - adds the in-line force spectrum -> Strouhal number
import glob
import os

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

OUT = "paper"
L = 0.60                 # submerged length (m)  -- CHECK, see draft
TANK_W, TANK_H = 0.90, 0.75
G = 9.81
T0, T1 = 3.0, 8.0        # steady averaging window (s)
FS = 200.0
EXCLUDE = {17: "zero drifted ~4.2 N during/after run"}

COLORS = {"1in": "#2a78d6", "1.5in": "#eb6834", "2in": "#1baf7a"}
MARKERS = {"1in": "o", "1.5in": "s", "2in": "^"}
SIZES = {"1in": 6, "1.5in": 5.5, "2in": 7.5}
LABELS = {"1in": "D = 25.4 mm", "1.5in": "D = 38.1 mm", "2in": "D = 50.8 mm"}
ORDER = ["1in", "1.5in", "2in"]
INK, MUTED, GRID = "#1f1f1e", "#6b6a63", "#e1e0d9"


def water_rho(T):
    # Tanaka et al. (2001), kg/m^3
    a1, a2, a3, a4, a5 = -3.983035, 301.797, 522528.9, 69.34881, 999.974950
    return a5 * (1 - (T + a1) ** 2 * (T + a2) / (a3 * (T + a4)))


def water_mu(T):
    # Vogel equation, Pa s
    return 2.414e-5 * 10 ** (247.8 / (T + 273.15 - 140.0))


def sensitivity(path):
    cal = pd.read_csv(path)
    p, cov = np.polyfit(cal.mass_g / 1000 * G, cal.voltage_V, 1, cov=True)
    resid = cal.voltage_V - np.polyval(p, cal.mass_g / 1000 * G)
    return p[0], np.sqrt(cov[0, 0]), np.abs(resid).max() / p[0]


def load(path):
    if "2026-03" in path:
        d = pd.read_csv(path, sep=";")
    else:
        d = pd.read_csv(path, comment="#")
    d.columns = ["t", "V"]
    return d


def re_axis(ax):
    ax.set_xscale("log")
    ax.set_xlim(4000, 60000)
    ticks = [5e3, 1e4, 2e4, 5e4]
    ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(matplotlib.ticker.FixedLocator(ticks))
    ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(matplotlib.ticker.FixedFormatter(
        ["5 000", "10 000", "20 000", "50 000"]))
    ax.xaxis.set_minor_formatter(matplotlib.ticker.NullFormatter())


def style(ax):
    for s in ("top", "right"):
        ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)
    for s in ("left", "bottom"):
        ax.spines[s].set_color("#c3c2b7")
    ax.tick_params(colors=MUTED, labelcolor=INK)
    ax.grid(True, color=GRID, lw=0.6)
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)


cal = {"2025-09": sensitivity("data/calibration/loadcell_2025-09.csv"),
       "2026-03": sensitivity("data/calibration/loadcell_2026-03.csv")}
log = pd.read_csv("data/run_log.csv").set_index("run_id")

rows = []
for f in sorted(glob.glob("data/raw/*/run_*.csv")):
    run = int(os.path.basename(f)[4:7])
    sens = cal["2026-03" if "2026-03" in f else "2025-09"][0]
    d = load(f)
    tare = d.V[d.t < 1.0].mean()
    F = (d.V - tare) / sens
    st = (d.t > T0) & (d.t < T1)
    x = (F[st] - F[st].mean()).values
    P = np.abs(np.fft.rfft(x * np.hanning(len(x)))) ** 2
    fr = np.fft.rfftfreq(len(x), 1 / FS)
    m = fr > 0.5
    rows.append({"run": run, "F_mean": F[st].mean(), "F_rms": F[st].std(),
                 "f_inline": fr[m][np.argmax(P[m])],
                 "zero_shift_N": (d.V[d.t > 11].mean() - tare) / sens})

df = pd.DataFrame(rows).join(log, on="run")
D = df.diameter_mm / 1000
U = df.speed_m_s
T = df.water_temp_c
df["rho"] = water_rho(T)
df["nu"] = water_mu(T) / df.rho
df["Re"] = U * D / df.nu
df["Re_20C"] = U * D / 1.004e-6
df["Cd"] = df.F_mean / (0.5 * df.rho * U ** 2 * D * L)
df["Cd_rms"] = df.F_rms / (0.5 * df.rho * U ** 2 * D * L)
df["St"] = df.f_inline / 2 * D / U          # in-line force oscillates at 2 f_s
df["Fr_D"] = U / np.sqrt(G * D)
df["blockage"] = D * L / (TANK_W * TANK_H)
df["L_over_D"] = L / D
df["excluded"] = df.run.isin(EXCLUDE)
df.round(5).to_csv(f"{OUT}/run_table.csv", index=False)

good = df[~df.excluded]
summ = good.groupby("cylinder").agg(
    D_mm=("diameter_mm", "first"), n=("run", "size"),
    Re_min=("Re", "min"), Re_max=("Re", "max"),
    T_mean=("water_temp_c", "mean"),
    Cd_mean=("Cd", "mean"), Cd_sd=("Cd", "std"),
    Cdrms_mean=("Cd_rms", "mean"),
    St_mean=("St", "mean"), St_sd=("St", "std"),
    blockage=("blockage", "first"), L_over_D=("L_over_D", "first"),
    FrD_max=("Fr_D", "max")).loc[ORDER]
summ["Cd_sem"] = summ.Cd_sd / np.sqrt(summ.n)
summ.round(4).to_csv(f"{OUT}/summary_table.csv")

pd.set_option("display.width", 200)
print("calibration (sens V/N, se, max resid N):")
for k, v in cal.items():
    print(f"  {k}: {v[0]:.6f} +/- {v[1]:.6f}, {v[2]:.4f} N")
print(df[["run", "cylinder", "speed_m_s", "water_temp_c", "Re", "Re_20C", "Cd",
          "Cd_rms", "St", "Fr_D", "zero_shift_N"]].round(4).to_string())
print(summ.round(4).to_string())
print("all good runs: Cd = %.3f +/- %.3f (sd), St = %.3f +/- %.3f"
      % (good.Cd.mean(), good.Cd.std(), good.St.mean(), good.St.std()))
print("Re over/under-estimate with 20 C nu: %.1f%% to %.1f%%"
      % ((df.Re_20C / df.Re - 1).min() * 100, (df.Re_20C / df.Re - 1).max() * 100))
# linear trend of Cd with log10(Re) for each cylinder
for c in ORDER:
    g = good[good.cylinder == c]
    p = np.polyfit(np.log10(g.Re), g.Cd, 1)
    print(f"  {c}: dCd/dlog10Re = {p[0]:.3f}")
# Welch t between 1in and 2in
a, b = good[good.cylinder == "1in"].Cd, good[good.cylinder == "2in"].Cd
t = (b.mean() - a.mean()) / np.sqrt(a.var() / len(a) + b.var() / len(b))
print(f"2in - 1in: dCd = {b.mean() - a.mean():.3f}, Welch t = {t:.2f}")
r17 = df[df.run == 17].iloc[0]
print(f"run 17 Cd (excluded) = {r17.Cd:.3f}")

# ---- Figure 1: example force trace + spectrum (run 5)
d = load("data/raw/2025-10-14/run_005.csv")
F = (d.V - d.V[d.t < 1].mean()) / cal["2025-09"][0]
st = (d.t > T0) & (d.t < T1)
x = (F[st] - F[st].mean()).values
P = np.abs(np.fft.rfft(x * np.hanning(len(x)))) ** 2
fr = np.fft.rfftfreq(len(x), 1 / FS)
fig, (a1, a2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(7.2, 2.8),
                             gridspec_kw={"width_ratios": [1.6, 1]})
a1.axvspan(T0, T1, color="#efeee9", lw=0)
a1.plot(d.t, F, color=COLORS["1in"], lw=0.6)
a1.text((T0 + T1) / 2, F.max() * 1.08, "averaging window", ha="center",
        color=MUTED, fontsize=8)
a1.set_xlabel("$t$ (s)"); a1.set_ylabel("$F_D$ (N)")
a1.set_ylim(-0.3, F.max() * 1.2)
a2.semilogy(fr, P / P.max(), color=COLORS["1in"], lw=1)
a2.set_xlim(0, 40); a2.set_ylim(1e-6, 2)
fpk = fr[fr > 0.5][np.argmax(P[fr > 0.5])]
a2.annotate(f"{fpk:.1f} Hz = $2f_s$", (fpk, 1), (fpk + 6, 0.2), color=INK,
            fontsize=8, arrowprops={"arrowstyle": "-", "color": MUTED, "lw": 0.6})
a2.set_xlabel("$f$ (Hz)"); a2.set_ylabel("normalised PSD")
for ax, lab in ((a1, "(a)"), (a2, "(b)")):
    style(ax)
    ax.text(-0.02, 1.04, lab, transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=9, color=INK)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(f"{OUT}/fig1_trace_spectrum.png", dpi=200)
fig.savefig(f"{OUT}/fig1_trace_spectrum.pdf")

# ---- Figure 2: Cd vs Re
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.2, 3.6))
for c in ORDER:
    g = good[good.cylinder == c]
    ax.plot(g.Re, g.Cd, MARKERS[c], ms=SIZES[c], color=COLORS[c], mec="white",
            mew=1.0, label=LABELS[c])
ax.plot(r17.Re, r17.Cd, MARKERS["2in"], ms=SIZES["2in"], mfc="none", mec=COLORS["2in"],
        mew=1.0, label="run 17 (excluded)")
re_axis(ax)
ax.set_xlabel("$Re = UD/\\nu$"); ax.set_ylabel("$C_D$")
ax.set_ylim(0.9, 1.45)
style(ax)
ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8, loc="upper left", labelcolor=INK)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(f"{OUT}/fig2_cd_vs_re.png", dpi=200)
fig.savefig(f"{OUT}/fig2_cd_vs_re.pdf")

# ---- Figure 3: St vs Re
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.2, 3.2))
for c in ORDER:
    g = good[good.cylinder == c]
    ax.plot(g.Re, g.St, MARKERS[c], ms=SIZES[c], color=COLORS[c], mec="white",
            mew=1.0, label=LABELS[c])
ax.axhline(0.2, color=MUTED, lw=0.8, ls="--")
re_axis(ax)
ax.set_ylim(0.15, 0.25)
ax.set_xlabel("$Re$"); ax.set_ylabel("$St = f_s D/U$")
style(ax)
ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8, loc="lower center", ncol=3, labelcolor=INK)
fig.tight_layout()

fig.savefig(f"{OUT}/fig3_strouhal.pdf")
